title: I confronted religious merchants in Kaduna to achieve peace — Uba Sani
excerpt: For years, Kaduna State was synonymous with ethno-religious violence, communal distrust, and bloodshed, with successive administrations struggling to end the cycle of killings t...
description: For years, Kaduna State was synonymous with ethno-religious violence, communal distrust, and bloodshed, with successive administrations struggling to end the cycle of killings t...
content:
For years, Kaduna State was synonymous with ethno-religious violence, communal distrust, and bloodshed, with successive administrations struggling to end the cycle of killings that fractured communities and undermined the state’s economic and social life. But Governor Uba Sani believes the tide has turned, insisting that the peace being experienced in the state is the product of deliberate efforts to dismantle what he calls the “merchants of ethno-religious crises,” promote inclusive governance, and address the economic conditions that fuel insecurity. From Southern Kaduna to Birnin Gwari, he says, the emphasis has been on rebuilding trust, taking development to neglected communities, and making citizens see one another as partners rather than adversaries.

When we came in, the first thing we looked at was recognising the fact that our state is the most diverse state in Nigeria. Of course, I agree with you that the number of lives we lost in Kaduna in the last 20 years, before we came, was more than the number of lives lost because of insurgency, kidnapping, and banditry. Knowing that, we believed that for us to claim any success as a government, we must bring our people together.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

The only way we could do that was by ensuring that we created a state where everyone would be carried along in whatever we were doing. Of course, we decided to run a system that would bring everyone together, which is a highly inclusive government. For us, inclusivity isn’t just about bringing people to sit with us. It’s about taking development to every part of Kaduna State. When we came in, we looked at the deficits in terms of infrastructure, healthcare, and education. We looked at this holistically, and we believed it was the only way we could address injustice and marginalisation. Some people felt they were not treated like citizens of our state.

We believed that doing that really demanded that we relegate politics and elevate governance. Doing that, of course, could sometimes be difficult because when you are elected as a governor, you have people who work with you. The first thing they tell you is to consider people who voted for you and ignore those who did not. But when we came in, it was not about who voted for us and who did not; it wasn’t the issue at all. It was about carrying everyone along. So, we really tried to put that aside and focus on carrying everyone along, including those who did not vote for us. We took development to every part of Kaduna State, irrespective of party, religious, or ethnic affiliation.

Of course, a lot of people have been talking about the Kaduna Model, asking how we did it. That is because in the last three and a half years in Kaduna, we have not experienced a single ethno-religious crisis, which is highly unprecedented. But for me, the Kaduna Model is nothing difficult. It’s about running a state where you carry everyone along and, as much as possible, be fair to everyone. Of course, human beings want justice. Sometimes you might work with people who are certainly merchants. When I say merchants, I mean people who only survive whenever there is an ethno-religious crisis. You have to eliminate them within the system.

If you don’t eliminate them within the system, the problem will continue. We tried as much as possible to eliminate those merchants, which was actually very difficult. That was because some of them also felt they were part of the system, and they also helped to win the election. That was the first battle you have to encounter as a leader.

Yes, ethno-religious merchants. For me, it takes a lot of political will to do that because they also feel they have a stake. Probably some of them contributed significantly to making one win the election. But then, along that line, of course, I had issues with many people who probably misunderstood my ideology. I tried to explain to some that they need to go back. Happily, I look at my antecedents. I am not just a normal politician.

I’m someone who spent many years fighting for justice, equality, democracy, and the rule of law. So, putting my ideology aside is very difficult. I paid my dues. I went to detention five times fighting for democracy in Nigeria. I was in the Senate. I would have been comfortable. But I decided to contest for the governorship of my state simply because I wasn’t happy about how toxic our state was. People didn’t trust one another. I was not comfortable with how the state was divided along the locations where people lived. People go to work together and eat together as family and friends. But when they close their offices, they go to different places because nobody trusts one another.

I felt Kaduna State was the most important city in all of Northern Nigeria.

At that time, I believed the only thing we needed to do was restore the glory of our state. Today, I’m happy. Gradually, we are restoring the glory of our state. Everyone now feels comfortable. Everyone wants to stay in Kaduna. That was the reason why, when the president wanted to launch his campaign, he chose Kaduna. The Kaduna of the past is different from the Kaduna of today. Everyone feels Kaduna is home now. We quickly abolished the issue of citizen and indigene dichotomy because our strength is in our diversity. But most importantly, we are highly cosmopolitan. That is the reason we don’t look at things through the lenses of religion, geography, or ethnicity.

Yes, I can say that largely. But I still believe we can do more, simply because we cannot rest. We must consolidate. When I say merchants, the merchants are not going to give up. I’m not sure we have completely defeated them. We have done a lot. If we rest, they will take us back. I remember when we were trying to choose our deputy governor; a lot of people thought it was difficult. But I said, no, this is a new Kaduna. Nobody will worry about whether it is a Muslim or a Christian. We have moved beyond that. When we decided to make a decision, people thought there would be issues. Nobody said a word. In three years, we have done a lot to promote interfaith harmony in our state.

All the leaders of both religions who didn’t sit at the same table now sit together. They understand poverty has no ethnic or tribal mark. It has no respect for religion or ethnicity. The poor man is a poor man. The only thing is that they believe we need to work together. They put that aside and now think about how to move us forward. Because at the end of the day, the elites still live together. It’s only the poor people who are separated.

Who is really working to ensure the poor people remain separated? It is the elites. It was an easy decision to say, look, the elites cannot live together while the poor people live separately. You cannot do that. I will not accept that. When I came in, in the first month, I was giving people a lot of land. There were some I gave land to in a particular place. They sold it because they said they could not live in such a place.

Today, I’m working to ensure that everyone lives together. Just like the people living together, the downtrodden must also live together without suspicion. For me, in Kaduna, it is not the number of bridges we built. It’s not the number of roads we constructed. It’s about the unity of our state. Like I always say, Kaduna is not only the political capital of Northern Nigeria; it’s both a political and spiritual capital, I can tell you for free. That’s the reason why, whenever there’s any religious crisis in Kaduna, virtually everything within the Middle Belt and even the far North-East may be affected.

In the last three years, there were some religious crises in Benue and Plateau, but there was nothing in Kaduna. If it happens in Kaduna, it will happen in several states. But it could happen anywhere; it will not come to Kaduna. That is how strategic Kaduna is. It is the heartbeat of the Middle Belt in Nigeria. People don’t understand that. A lot of people never gave us a chance. But we said, look, it was not an issue that happened spontaneously. It’s a creation of some selfish politicians who divided our people to achieve their selfish political aims.

That was easy for us because the only way to demolish it was to not do what they used to do—to let people understand that we must live together as one family.

I just talked about merchants. Maybe you have to understand what I mean by merchants. You can do something in other states, and it’s fine, but in Kaduna it’s not possible. If you go to the media house and insult Uba Sani one million times, I will thank you for that because this is democracy. I also challenged successive military governments, and I paid the price by going to prison. But look, what we have done in Kaduna—and I made it clear, and I still have no apology—is that in Kaduna, because of our diversity, you cannot come and say anything to incite the people. I’m fighting the merchants, and I will continue to fight them because I realise that the reason for all those religious crises is that the merchants create problems while innocent people in the villages die. I made it clear.

Talk politics, but don’t talk about ethno-religious issues in Kaduna. I have looked through the constitution as a civil rights activist for many years, and I have not seen where freedom of speech has given me the right to say something that can result in the loss of lives of innocent and gullible people who are not educated. I don’t believe in that. If it happens, honestly speaking, I will certainly go after that person. I said it many times. I have no apology for that. But if you go and say, I’m against this party, it’s okay. But as long as I always wake up in the morning and go through my oath, and I read my oath every two or three days, I see that it is my responsibility to protect the lives and properties of the people of Kaduna.

If you come to say anything that can affect the lives and properties of innocent people, honestly speaking, I will go after you. I fought for the rule of law in this country. You see, I’m not just a normal activist. If you ask any activist in Nigeria, I was probably the closest to Chief Gani Fawehinmi. You can ask anyone. Chief Gani always told us, honestly speaking, at the heat of the struggle, that we can do anything. If you are someone groomed by Gani like me, who lived in his house for four years, you would agree with me that our training by Chief Gani was to respect constituted authority. Gani would be arrested today by the police.

Tomorrow, he would come out, and we would write a statement against the police; he would tell us to drop it. We would ask him why, and he would say, as we are sitting now in my parlour eating, someone called you and said that somebody is getting into your house, and the lives of your family and your wife were under threat. Who would you call? We would say the police. Then he would ask: Why do you want to destroy them? It is their job. For me, that was my training. That’s how I was groomed. I believe in the rule of law. If you do something that can affect the lives of innocent people, as a governor, I will just allow the law to take its course. If you go to court, you will sort it out because I am not a judge. I will help you to face the judiciary, certainly. If you have a good lawyer, fine.

If you don’t have a good lawyer, sort it out. I’m not apologising for this. And that’s the reason why I’m keeping Kaduna safe. If I had not done that, I can tell you, the merchants would have defeated us. And if the merchants defeated us, today, I wouldn’t have been going to Southern Kaduna. For the last six months, when I went to Birnin Gwari, I stopped on the road. I saw farmers in the market. Ten metres away, there were more than 200 cows. I asked them if they were not the ones killing themselves before, and they said yes. I said, why did you stop? One of them said they no longer see the people who were instigating them. If you move from there to the Southern part of Kaduna, where people died every day, nobody is dying.

The farmers are there. The cows are there. Why are they not fighting? It is because I’m destroying the merchants one by one, and I’ll continue to destroy them. One merchant could ruin the lives of 1,000 innocent people.

Birnin Gwari is a clear case study. It wasn’t rocket science. Birnin Gwari was the epicentre of insurgency in the whole of Nigeria. I went to Birnin Gwari and met the Emir. The Emir of Birnin Gwari had been there for almost 40 years. I told him, why is it that people are being kidnapped every day in this place? When I was in the Senate, I represented the central zone. Every day, in the National Assembly, we stood up for a minute of silence because people had lost their lives. I made an effort to create state police. It was my bill in the Senate. I was defeated. We moved on.

But in the absence of state police, which I believe was the only solution, there must be another solution. We had to look at the symptoms and drivers of insecurity. There must be symptoms. What are the symptoms? What are the drivers? You have to study it holistically. The insecurity in the Northwestern part of Nigeria has no relationship with the insecurity in the North-East. That’s the first thing.

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

On insecurity, you have to understand that the North-East is largely ideological. The North-West is poverty and economy. Instead of successive governments resolving it, they didn’t do that. It also created a trust deficit between the people and government.

You must allow the process to be driven by the communities because they don’t trust government any longer. That’s what we meant. And I asked them what they wanted. I don’t pay ransom. I don’t know bandits. The Emir of Birnin Gwari told me every bandit around the area was born in Birnin Gwari in his presence. The solution became nearer. Most bandits in his area are under the age of 40. They were born while he was watching them. I said, what is the problem? He said the problem was the economy. He said two major markets—the grains market and the livestock market—were closed for nine years.

No government could open them. I went there and said I wanted to open the markets. I opened the markets. But I told them I had a condition. As we were speaking at the time, 222 people in Birnin Gwari were already with the bandits. I told them that I would open the market, but ensure that in the next one week, the 222 would be released. Because he knew the parents of the bandits, he intervened. We opened the markets. Within five days, all the captives were released. That was the first step. The second step was asking the Emir of Birnin Gwari what he needed again. At that time, most of the schools were closed. All their hospitals were closed because of bandits.

We opened all the schools. The market started booming. As I’m speaking with you, every day you can go to Birnin Gwari. One farmer made N1.7 billion from grains. Now in Birnin Gwari, every day you have lorries filled with maize and other grains, numbering about 35, going to Lagos. In addition, more than 50 trucks of cows go to Lagos. They even requested a new market.

I’m building a new grain market and a new livestock market, the biggest ever in Kaduna. As we are speaking, Birnin Gwari has not seen one kilometre of road in 20 years. I had to take the CGC, the company constructing roads in Abuja, to construct 36 kilometres of road in Birnin Gwari, cutting across 77 farming communities. They’ve never seen that in their lives. Nobody wants to kidnap any more.

Yes, because it’s the economy. That’s number one. We took the same model to other areas and resolved the issues there. That’s the reason we were able to reclaim 500,000 hectares of abandoned farmland. Last year, when people wanted to go to Mecca, I was telling Mr President that the Chairman of the Hajj Commission wrote letters to all the states that we should subsidise the Hajj. I said I don’t subsidise going to Hajj. I build roads in Kaduna. For that reason, even for me as a Muslim, it is clear. If you cannot afford it, you don’t have to go. I didn’t subsidise it.

The chairman of the Hajj Commission came back to me after the deadline was over and told me Kaduna is still number one in Nigeria. And I said, do you know why we’re number one? I said, the economy is booming.

The farmers come to farms. When I look at the analysis, 70 per cent are farmers from rural areas, not even in the town. The people in the town are poor. The people in the metropolitan part of Kaduna, the city, are poor. The rich ones are in the rural areas. Not only that; that is why, out of the 1,315 kilometres being constructed in Kaduna, 800 kilometres are in the rural areas, connecting farms with markets. It was largely the economy.

How much was the budget for agriculture when we came in? N1.4 billion. Today, the budget for agriculture in Kaduna is N110 billion. We surpassed the Malabo Declaration of 2014 of 10 per cent. We’re at 12 per cent. We’re leading Nigeria in agriculture. That’s why we were the first state in Nigeria to launch our SAPZ, Special Agro-Processing Zone. Not only that; we were the second state in the whole of Nigeria to have an agricultural quality centre, where we can have all our grains certified for exportation.

On transportation, when Makinde opened his bus terminal, there were about a thousand buses. We are concluding ours next month. The President promised to commission it. There are 5,000 buses. It’s the biggest ultra-modern bus terminal in Nigeria. When Sardauna was alive, he built Ahmadu Bello Stadium in 1964. It was one of the leading stadiums, apart from the national stadium in Lagos. Then the one in Kaduna was one of the two major stadiums hosting FIFA tournaments. Ahmadu Bello Stadium deteriorated and became obsolete.

The last time we hosted any FIFA event in Kaduna was almost 2016, right? It was a junior football tournament. I went to the president and told him the dream of Sardauna was destroyed. I said we needed to bring back Ahmadu Bello Stadium. He said, what do we do?



---

### 🎙️ Perspectives & What Comes Next

He said, what do you want, Comrade? I said, give it to me. He said, what do you want to do? I said, Mr President, I will demolish it. As we are speaking, Ahmadu Bello Stadium has been demolished. I am rebuilding it into a 33,000-capacity stadium to be completed in December. It will be the only stadium with a hybrid pitch. Uyo is grass. The stadium here is grass. To put a hybrid pitch alone is over N2 billion. We are gradually bringing glory.

I told Mr President that the just-concluded FIFA tournament in the US fetched $24 billion. Morocco, at the last AFCON, made $1.6 billion. The new stadium we are constructing would generate revenue and contribute to the economy.

content:
itel Energy, a clean energy and power solutions brand, has promised to repair or replace faulty solar power equipment within 48 hours for customers across Nigeria as part of its after-sales support.

The company reemphasized their commitment during the Nigeria Energy exhibition week in Lagos, where it showcased new products and showed distributors, installers, both new and existing customers how its after-sales service works.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

The company said it offers remote services, home visits and product replacement where necessary.

According to the company, after-sales service is an important consideration for households and businesses switching from petrol and diesel generators to solar power, because a faulty inverter or battery can disrupt electricity supply and business operations.

Speaking on the sidelines at the exhibition, the Chief Executive Officer and Co-Founder of SunFi, a major distributor of itel Energy products, Rotimi Thomas, said the commitment boosted customers’ confidence in the products distributed through the company.

“The 48-hour resolution commitment from itel Energy is very important for us as a distribution platform because we don’t make the product and when a consumer buys a product through SunFi, they’re actually really buying a trusted service,” Thomas said.

He explained that customers needed assurance that equipment would be repaired or replaced when problems arose, rather than being left to deal with faults after purchase.

“That trust comes from the type of equipment that we use and the promise of being able to replace or repair the assets when there’s a problem,” he said.

Thomas also urged customers to look beyond warranty periods when choosing solar equipment, saying the speed and quality of support during the warranty period were equally important.

“But even more important than that five-year warranty is what happens before the five years or during the five-year period. How do you respond when I report that I have a problem with the product now?”

Thomas said the cost of solar systems remained a barrier to adoption, adding that the company offers instalment payment plans for households and businesses unable to pay the full amount.

According to him, about 30 to 40 per cent of prospective customers still request payment plans, which shows the need for financing options that make clean energy more accessible.

He said some customers preferred to pay between 10 and 30 per cent upfront and spread the balance over three, six, 12 or 24 months, or longer.

Meanwhile, itel Energy’s Country Service Manager, Emmanuel Kumuyi, said most common complaints reported by customers included overloading, protection issues and incorrect installation.

He said some problems arose when solar panels, inverters and batteries were not properly matched to the user’s power requirements.

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

Kumuyi advised customers to use certified engineers for installation and to ensure that their systems were correctly configured.

He explained that when a customer reports a fault, the company’s service agents document the complaint and refer it to an engineer for remote assistance.

According to him, if the problem cannot be resolved remotely, an engineer is assigned to visit the customer’s premises.

Where necessary, component or product replacement is initiated in line with the applicable warranty terms.

The company’s National Distributor Manager, Lucky Ovenseri, said itel Energy had distribution coverage across Nigeria’s 36 states, with showrooms and dedicated energy after-sales centres in major cities, including Lagos, Abuja, Port Harcourt, Ibadan and Kano.

He said the company also operated a replacement policy under which customers could receive another unit while their faulty equipment was being handled.

At the exhibition, itel Energy showcased its newly launched PowerTank 1000 and IP54 11kW Hybrid Inverter, targeting customers with different electricity needs.



---

### 🎙️ Perspectives & What Comes Next

The PowerTank 1000 demonstration featured a powered mini-chiller and a water dispenser, while visitors interested in the 11kW hybrid inverter sought information about pricing, installation, warranty coverage and its ability to support higher power demands.

The company currently has 5 Flagship service centers, and over 200 service centers across more than 60 cities, backed by Carlcare and Transsion Group’s network of 2,000+ service centers spread across Sub-saharan Africa,Middle-East,and Asia.

title: Arsenal End 14-Year Winless Run At Anfield To Go Top Of Premier League
excerpt: Arsenal moved to the top of the Premier League with their first win away to Liverpool in 14 years as Kai Havertz’s early strike secured a 1-0 victory for the Gunners.
description: Arsenal moved to the top of the Premier League with their first win away to Liverpool in 14 years as Kai Havertz’s early strike secured a 1-0 victory for the Gunners.
content:
Arsenal moved to the top of the Premier League with their first win away to Liverpool in 14 years as Kai Havertz’s early strike secured a 1-0 victory for the Gunners.

The defending champions were made to suffer after the German’s 16th-minute opener but held out for what could be a telling win in their quest to retain the title.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

Arsenal climbed three points clear of Manchester City at the top of the table.

But with City expected to be hit with a severe points penalty, unless they can overturn a guilty verdict on over 100 charges of breaking Premier League rules, Arsenal dealt a huge blow to their most likely rivals for the title.

“It’s been such a long time without this feeling here, that we really needed it,” said Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta. “We are extremely proud of what the team, the players, everybody has done.”

Liverpool produced arguably their best spell of Andoni Iraola’s early months in charge with a blistering 30 minutes after conceding, but failed to take their chances as the Spaniard suffered just his second defeat in 14 games since arriving from Bournemouth.

Arteta was stinging in his criticism of the Arsenal side that crashed out to fourth-tier Fleetwood on Tuesday in one of the biggest ever League Cup shocks.

The Arsenal boss got the response he desired in a strong start from the champions.

Havertz was one of the biggest culprits for wasting chances in midweek but made amends with a simple finish from Declan Rice’s precise low cross.

The early goal lit the touchpaper for a pulsating first 45 minutes as Liverpool roared back.

Iraola and Arteta played together as boys for Basque side Antiguoko Kirol Elkartea.

Arteta’s old friend gave his side one of the most uncomfortable afternoons they have experienced in recent seasons as Arsenal’s rock-solid defence was left clinging on for half-time.

“I loved the reaction from my players after going 1-0 down,” said Iraola. “I loved a lot of moments of the game.

“We have to keep going. It is very early in the season. Arsenal are in the best of the situations but it is just the start of November today.”

---

title: ‘Convert Our Diversity Into Prosperity,’ Tinubu Prays At Dinner With Nigerian Delegation In Mecca

content:
President Bola Tinubu has prayed for Nigeria’s diversity to become a source of prosperity, unity, peace and sustainable development for the benefit of all citizens.

The President made the prayer on Sunday in Mecca, Saudi Arabia, while hosting members of his delegation to dinner, according to a statement by his spokesperson, Bayo Onanuga.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

He expressed hope that Nigeria’s ethnic, religious and cultural diversity would remain a source of strength and national development rather than division, urging citizens to embrace mutual understanding, peaceful coexistence and a shared commitment to the country’s progress.

“May Almighty Allah bless Nigeria, convert our diversity into prosperity as a country,” Tinubu said.

He also prayed for enduring peace and harmony in the country, asking Allah to grant Nigeria’s leaders the wisdom, courage and foresight to steer the nation towards greater development and improved living conditions.

The President further sought divine guidance and protection for Nigerians at home and abroad, praying that Allah would strengthen the bonds of brotherhood among citizens and inspire patriotism, compassion and service to the nation.

Tinubu said Nigeria’s abundant human and natural resources, alongside the talents, creativity and enterprise of its diverse population, provided a strong foundation for building a prosperous and inclusive country.

He urged Nigerians of all faiths and backgrounds to continue working together in the national interest, expressing confidence that the country would overcome its challenges through faith, unity of purpose and collective determination.

Chairman of BUA Group, Abdulsamad Rabiu, reaffirmed his support for the President, saying the dinner provided another opportunity to pray for Nigeria’s peace, unity and prosperity.

“Today is actually the third dinner we’re having with His Excellency Mr President since we came to Makkah on Thursday night or Friday morning when Mr President arrived,” he said.

Rabiu said the discussions centred on praying for the country and appreciating Tinubu’s commitment to Nigeria.

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

“We will continue to support His Excellency in whatever capacity we can and definitely, as you all know, Mr President is very passionate about the country. He’s working very hard, and we’ll continue to support him,” he added.

Kwara State Governor and Chairman of the Nigerian Governors’ Forum, AbdulRahman AbdulRazaq, also praised the President’s commitment to building a united and prosperous nation.

“Only Allah can reward you; we will continue to pray for you daily and pray for Nigeria that you lead. May Allah continue to strengthen you in making the right decisions, strengthen your wisdom, your boldness, your audacity, your courage. May Allah lead you to the right path,” he said.

The Attorney-General of the Federation and Minister of Justice, Lateef Fagbemi, also prayed for Allah to strengthen the President in his efforts to deliver governance and justice to Nigerians, irrespective of their religious or ethnic backgrounds.

The dinner was attended by Yobe State Governor Mai Mala Buni; Kaduna State Governor Uba Sani; Jigawa State Governor Mohammed Namadi; Sokoto State Governor Ahmed Aliyu; and Borno State Governor Babagana Umara Zulum.

title: AI-Generated Photos: We Are Already Cleaning Up Our Register – INEC
excerpt: The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) says it has commenced the process of cleaning up its preliminary Register of Voters following the identification of records ...
description: The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) says it has commenced the process of cleaning up its preliminary Register of Voters following the identification of records ...
content:
The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) says it has commenced the process of cleaning up its preliminary Register of Voters following the identification of records with suspected AI-generated photographs and other irregularities.

The commission’s Director of Information and Communication Technology, Lawrence Bayode, said on Channels Television’s Sunday Politics that its Automated Biometric Identification System (ABIS) had flagged 268 records for review.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

“What we are currently doing now is looking at all these 268 records that ABIS already flagged as AI-generated or even something of irregularities,” he said.

Bayode explained that some people allegedly used their official credentials to create questionable profiles, exploiting a registration option designed for persons with disabilities who do not have complete fingers or have no fingers.

According to him, the option, known as special registration, was used to deceive the system and was among the irregularities detected by ABIS.

He said the commission had begun cleaning up the affected records.

“Those that we have seen, we are cleaning up,” Bayode said.

However, he clarified that not every photograph enhanced with artificial intelligence would be removed, distinguishing between images generated entirely by AI and genuine photographs improved with AI tools on mobile phones.

“Those that we know it is the AI on the phone that helped enhance their pictures, we can’t exclude such people because it was the AI on the phone that does that. Such people will still be on the register but those AI-generated, those photographs, all these will be removed. We are already looking at them,” he said.

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

The controversy followed the publication of INEC’s preliminary Register of Voters online on October 26, after screenshots circulated on social media showing questionable photographs attached to voter records, including entries from parts of Edo State.

The concerns also included allegations of duplicate entries and reports that names of deceased persons appeared on the register.

In response, INEC said the online version was the same preliminary register displayed physically at Registration Areas nationwide from October 9 to 15. It explained that the publication did not reflect all the data-cleanup activities already in progress.

The commission also said the register was not yet the final certified version and that the display, claims and objections exercise was designed to allow members of the public to identify inaccuracies and questionable entries before certification.



---

### 🎙️ Perspectives & What Comes Next

INEC has said it will complete the necessary verification, adjudication and data-cleanup processes before certifying the final Register of Voters on December 15, 2026.

title: Tinubu’s 2023 Electricity Pledge Taken Out Of Context, Says APC Campaign Council
excerpt: The All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council has defended President Bola Tinubu’s 2023 campaign promise to end estimated billing and ensure stable electrici...
description: The All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council has defended President Bola Tinubu’s 2023 campaign promise to end estimated billing and ensure stable electrici...
content:
The All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council has defended President Bola Tinubu’s 2023 campaign promise to end estimated billing and ensure stable electricity supply, saying his remarks have been taken out of context.

In a statement on Sunday, the council’s spokesperson, Dele Alake, said Tinubu made the pledge while addressing members of the Organised Private Sector (OPS) in Lagos ahead of the 2023 general elections.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

Alake said the then presidential candidate had outlined plans to address longstanding structural and institutional challenges in the power sector, particularly the burden of estimated billing on households and businesses.

He recalled Tinubu’s words at the meeting: “Whichever way, by all means necessary, you will have electricity, and you will not pay for estimated bills anymore. A promise made will be a promise kept.

“If I don’t keep the promise and I come for a second term, don’t vote for me, unless I give you adequate reasons why I couldn’t deliver.”

The APC spokesperson argued that some recent commentaries had omitted the concluding part of the statement, in which Tinubu said he would provide Nigerians with adequate reasons if he failed to fulfil the pledge before seeking a second term.

He maintained that the president’s commitment should be assessed alongside his administration’s interventions in the electricity sector since assuming office in 2023.

According to Alake, Tinubu signed the Electricity Act 2023 on June 9, less than two weeks after taking office, allowing state governments to participate in electricity generation, transmission and distribution.

He listed Lagos, Enugu, Abia, Ekiti, Oyo, Kaduna and Niger among the states that have established electricity regulatory agencies to take advantage of the legislation and attract private investment.

On metering, Alake said the administration launched the Presidential Metering Initiative to address a backlog of more than seven million unmetered electricity customers, adding that over 1.5 million customers had been metered under the programme in the last three years.

He also said the government had taken steps to address more than ₦6 trillion in legacy debts accumulated between 2015 and 2025, while introducing a ₦4 trillion bond programme to settle verified obligations to power generation and gas companies.

The spokesperson said the first and second tranches of the bond programme had raised more than ₦1.2 trillion towards settling the debts owed to 21 generation companies and gas suppliers.

Alake further listed investments in substations, grid expansion and renewable energy projects among the administration’s efforts to improve electricity supply.

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

He said the Rural Electrification Agency had connected universities, hospitals and rural communities to solar power, while the government had unveiled plans to modernise the Osogbo Grid Control Centre and construct an East-West super grid.

On transmission infrastructure, he said the administration reviewed the Presidential Power Initiative inherited from the late President Muhammadu Buhari and signed an acceleration agreement with its German partners in December 2023.

He added that the Federal Executive Council approved the first batch of five Transmission Company of Nigeria substations for upgrades in December 2024, with another set of projects approved in June 2026 to construct eight new substations and upgrade four existing ones.

Alake said the administration had also introduced different electricity service bands and adjusted tariffs towards cost-reflective levels to improve the financial position of distribution companies, while putting measures in place to protect low-income households.

He acknowledged that efforts to resolve the power sector crisis were still ongoing but insisted that Tinubu remained committed to his campaign promise.



---

### 🎙️ Perspectives & What Comes Next

“As he seeks Nigerians’ mandate for a second term in office, he will proudly present his scorecard in the power sector and clearly tell Nigerians what remains to be done,” he said.

Iran’s Revolutionary Guards said on Thursday that three oil tankers had caught fire after hitting mines while attempting to cross the Strait of Hormuz.

“Over the past 24 hours, three violating oil tankers exploded and caught fire after striking mines while attempting to pass through the unauthorised southern route of the Strait of Hormuz,” the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said in a statement.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

The vessels had “switched off all their radar and navigation systems” and disregarded warnings from the IRGC navy, the statement said.

It was not immediately clear when the incidents occurred or which flags the tankers were flying.

Since the outbreak of the war on February 28, Iran has severely restricted traffic through the strategic waterway, which normally carries about one-fifth of global oil and gas consumption.

The United States has in response imposed a blockade on Iranian ports.

Iran’s armed forces have repeatedly accused US Central Command (CENTCOM), which oversees US military operations in the region, of encouraging vessels to use a southern corridor near the Omani coast that Tehran considers unauthorised.

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

“The IRGC Navy states that the unauthorised route through the Strait of Hormuz is mined, and that vessel owners and crews are responsible for transiting these routes and should not pay attention to CENTCOM’s delusions on social media,” the statement said.

Earlier on Thursday, the British maritime agency UKMTO said it had received a report of a ship on fire in the strait but gave no details about the cause or any casualties.

It was not immediately clear if it was one of the three ships referred to by the Guards.



---

### 🎙️ Perspectives & What Comes Next

The organisation also said it had captured a US reconnaissance drone during an operation in the Strait of Hormuz in a separate statement.

“The IRGC Navy announced that its electronic warfare unit had successfully captured a US MQM-170 drone during an offensive operation in the western Strait of Hormuz,” the statement said.

content:
A young cyclist from Kebbi State, Bello Muhammad, has earned international recognition after riding a bicycle measuring 2.9 metres in height without assistance.

The achievement, recognised by Guinness World Records, was celebrated at the Kebbi State Government Secretariat in Birnin Kebbi, where officials commended the cyclist for showcasing the ingenuity and potential of Nigerian youths.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

At 2.9 metres tall, this bicycle has earned its rider, Bello Muhammad, a place in the Guinness World Records.

The Kebbi-born cyclist reportedly achieved the feat on September 22, 2026, in Kebbi State, by riding the towering bicycle unsupported.

Beyond the record, the achievement is drawing attention to the creativity, determination and technical ingenuity of young people in the state.

German car giant Volkswagen said it aims to export at least 300,000 vehicles made in China each year by 2030, as well as technologies it is developing in the country.

Europe’s biggest carmaker has been mired in crisis because of Chinese competition, weak demand in key markets and a choppy electric transition, and has launched a huge job-cutting drive.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

“Together we plan to export at least 300,000 cars a year by 2030, but our ambition goes beyond exporting vehicles,” Volkswagen Group’s China head Ralf Brandstatter said Wednesday on a trip to Hefei in eastern China, where the firm has a big R&D centre.

Volkswagen said that for the first time it will also export technology developed in Hefei to other parts of Asia, the Middle East and South America, but not Europe for now.

This includes the vehicles’ electronic architecture, developed with the help of Chinese company Xpeng.

It also includes its platform and driver-assistance system, produced with China’s Horizon Robotics.

The German firm hopes these innovations will help it overcome fierce competition and sluggish growth in China and other markets.

“What we develop in China makes Volkswagen more competitive around the world,” Brandstatter said.

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

“China-developed technologies are becoming a key part of the global setup of Volkswagen Group and a strategic advantage.”

The carmaker struck a deal in September with unions to cut 50,000 additional jobs by 2030, bringing its total planned workforce reduction to around 100,000.

Volkswagen’s reputation remains clouded by a massive 2015 fraud scandal uncovered when California regulators discovered that it had installed illegal software on millions of diesel-powered cars to cheat on emissions tests.



---

Rival Mercedes-Benz on Tuesday became the third of the big three German carmakers alongside Volkswagen and BMW to have issued a profit warning for the year, citing difficulties in China.

title: “Talent Is Not Enough”: Mr Eazi On The Shift From Pure Art To Algorithm-Driven Entertainment
excerpt: As the global footprint of African pop culture expands, industry stakeholders are confronting a fundamental economic reality: raw musical talent and viral singles are no longer ...
description: As the global footprint of African pop culture expands, industry stakeholders are confronting a fundamental economic reality: raw musical talent and viral singles are no longer ...
content:
As the global footprint of African pop culture expands, industry stakeholders are confronting a fundamental economic reality: raw musical talent and viral singles are no longer sufficient to sustain a modern creative enterprise in the algorithm era.

Speaking during an interview on The Beat 99.9 FM with Osi Dirisu, music entrepreneur and investor Oluwatosin Ajibade, widely known as Mr Eazi, dissected the evolving relationship between artistic creation and commercial entertainment, warning that passive consumer habits have fundamentally altered how music is marketed.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

While contrasting conceptual bodies of work—such as his 2023 critically acclaimed project The Evil Genius—with the daily demands of short-form video platforms, Ajibade argued that creators aiming for mainstream commercial success must look beyond traditional studio production.

“Culture keeps changing, but as an artist, your goal is to make the music,” Ajibade explained. “Once you make the music, you have already created your art. But it’s beyond that now—it’s not just art. There is art, and there is entertainment. Now we are in the era of entertainment because entertainment has been democratised.”

Addressing the shift in fan engagement, Ajibade pointed out that modern digital consumption often judges a song by its utility within user-generated content, such as TikTok dance challenges or lifestyle vlogs, rather than deep sonic appreciation.

While maintaining that purist art will always find its dedicated audience via algorithmic curation, he stressed that commercial pop music requires active multimedia engagement.

“If you as an artist just want to be an artist—you don’t want to entertain, you just want to do your art—there is still a place for that, and people will still find you,” he noted. “The algorithm will still send you to your people. But if you want the full suite of entertainment, then, my brother, talent is not enough.”

This structural shift in content consumption mirrors broader financial challenges across the African creative economy, particularly concerning capital acquisition and infrastructure development.

Over the past decade, major investments into the African music ecosystem—ranging from venture-backed artist incubators to institutional equity acquisitions in labels like Mavin Global—have largely been driven by international venture capital and foreign media conglomerates.

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

Addressing debates surrounding foreign capital dependency, Ajibade adopted a pragmatic stance, rejecting ideological resistance to international investment.

“Money is money, bro. I’m ready to take anybody’s money,” Ajibade asserted. “If people from Mars, Jupiter, or Venus say they want to invest, Baba, we go collect the money. We take it from everywhere; we accept all types of money for proper business.”

However, the entrepreneur emphasised that foreign interest should not absolve domestic financial institutions and high-net-worth individuals from investing in the continent’s creative architecture.

Historically, domestic private equity in Nigeria has heavily favoured traditional sectors like real estate, telecommunications, and energy, viewing entertainment and sports as high-risk novelties. Ajibade argued that early market-movers—including his own incubator models and subsequent external funding into Nigerian music companies—have provided a clear proof of concept that the creative sector is a high-yield asset class.



---

### 🎙️ Perspectives & What Comes Next

“There’s nothing wrong with money coming from outside, but I feel there is still a lot of work to be done in terms of putting money into our own entertainment structures,” he said. “Until Empawa came and put all that money into music, and people saw the results of those investments, other people couldn’t see the model. There are so many multi-millionaires and billionaires in Nigeria; hopefully now they can see that entertainment is not a joke—it is real business, and people can put money in it.”

The National President of the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC), Comrade Joe Ajaero, has condemned the position of the Trade Union Congress (TUC), following the rejection of the ₦70,000 transport intervention approved by the Federal Government for workers across all levels for six months.

Ajaero made the comments while appearing on Channels Television’s The Morning Brief on Thursday.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

The NLC President alleged that the Union backed out of the negotiation process that led to the 70k transport intervention and therefore has no right to reject what it never advocated for.

“The agreement was not signed by the Trade Union Congress; you don’t kick against something you did not negotiate or never asked for,” Ajero said.

Ajaero said he would have preferred a situation where TUC was negotiating for a higher intervention than what the NLC was asking, and the government would have harmonised both requests.

He alleged that the TUC president said the minimum wage would be due for negotiation in August 2027; however, the Nigerian Labour rejected that claim, citing that it was not in line with the position of the law.

“They threatened us and said they are not part of it,” Ajero said that the NLC is completely on its own with the 70k transport intervention and is surprised by TUC’s stand on what was secured for the workers of the Labour union.

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

Speaking about the welfare  of the workers under the Trade Union,  Ajero said, “he left them and never came out to say they needed one or two naira, and now that we are done with this negotiation, he is still free to agitate for one million naira but not to reject what we have gotten.”

He stated that the TUC had no power to reject the intervention secured by the sister union; rather, they should advocate for a higher amount in the face of increased suffering due to a rise in energy prices

The labour leader argued that getting an additional ₦70,000, which also doubles as the current national minimum wage, just a few months before the negotiation of the minimum wage, which is scheduled to take place in April 2027, makes the ₦70,000 transport intervention a major landmark achievement.

title: Why 5G remains out of reach for most Nigerians
excerpt: …High cost of devices, coverage remains uneven
description: …High cost of devices, coverage remains uneven
content:
…High cost of devices, coverage remains uneven

…As smartphone market contracts 11% amid rising device prices

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

…Africa’s budget smartphone shipments plunge 34% amid rising costsBy Juliet Umeh

Nigeria’s mobile market has shifted significantly towards newer network technologies over the past three years, but 5G remains out of reach for most consumers. High smartphone prices, uneven network coverage and rising infrastructure costs continue to limit adoption, despite growing demand for mobile data.

In May 2023, 2G accounted for 58.36 percent of reported mobile connections, while 4G represented 25.06 percent and 5G just 0.12 percent. By August 2026, 4G had become the leading technology at 54.77 percent, while 2G fell to 36.05 percent. 5G increased to 4.92 percent.

The data from the Nigerian Communications Commission, NCC, show progress but underline how slowly the newest technology is reaching the wider population.

Chief Technology Officer of NATCOM Development and Investment Limited, trading as NTEL, Kingsley Uwazie, said Nigerians had a strong appetite for data consumption, but the cost of accessing 5G remained a significant barrier.

“The 5G ecosystem is in its maturity phase. It has been proven that there is an appetite. Nigerians have an appetite to consume data. But there is a barrier to acquiring the devices and using the technology,” he said.

Consumers need 5G-enabled smartphones to access the technology, but rising device prices are making upgrades increasingly difficult, particularly for low-income earners.

Uwazie said 5G devices remained expensive despite subsidies offered by some operators.

“5G, at the moment, is not a cheap technology to deploy or to own. The cost of 5G devices has been high,” he said.He cited MTN Nigeria and Airtel Nigeria as operators subsidising selected devices, adding that a phone available for about N50, 000 with a subsidy could cost more than N200, 000 without it.

The affordability challenge has intensified as Nigeria’s smartphone market contracted by 11 percent in the second quarter of 2026, according to technology research firm Omdia. Rising memory-chip costs, partly linked to growing demand from artificial intelligence, AI, data centres, have increased pressure on manufacturers and consumers.

Across Africa, shipments of smartphones priced below $100 fell by 34 percent year-on-year during the quarter.

In Nigeria, a market assessment published by technology news platform Condia found that prices of selected Tecno, Infinix, Oppo and itel models increased between January and June 2026. The midpoint price of the itel S-Series Ultra rose from about N263, 500 to N316,400, while the Infinix Zero Series increased from approximately N550,000 to N637,500.

Omdia warned in June that Nigerian smartphone prices could rise by another 15 to 30 percent through the remainder of 2026 if component costs continued increasing.

These developments could discourage consumers from upgrading, slowing the growth of the 5G user base.Coverage remains uneven

Even consumers who can afford compatible devices may struggle to access reliable 5G connections because coverage varies by location.

MTN’s 2023 pilot announcement identified Lagos, Abuja, Port Harcourt, Ibadan, Kano, Owerri and Maiduguri as intended launch cities, subject to coverage. Airtel began its rollout in Lagos, Ogun, Rivers and the Federal Capital Territory, focusing on selected locations.

However, a rollout in a city or state does not guarantee availability in every neighbourhood.

A December 2025 report based on Ookla analysis put Lagos’s average 5G coverage gap at 55.4 percent, meaning a compatible phone could not connect to 5G for more than half of the measured time. The gap was approximately 50 percent for MTN and 77 percent for Airtel.

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

In Abuja, the average gap stood at 47.4 percent. These figures measure time-based access gaps, not the proportion of land without coverage, but they illustrate the difficulty consumers face in obtaining consistent service.

Expanding 5G requires substantial investment in network infrastructure, electricity and transmission. Operators must determine whether the number of potential subscribers in an area can justify those costs.

Uwazie estimated that operating a telecommunications site in Nigeria could cost between $2,000 and $3,000 monthly, compared with about $300 in China and $500 in India. He said the costs included power and transmission.

“If you deploy 5G in areas where only two people have 5G-enabled phones, it means those two people can’t cater for the operating expenditure required to deploy 5G. The operating expenditure of running mobile networks in Nigeria is extremely high. It is a combination of both power and transmission, keeping that site up.”

The limited number of compatible devices can, therefore, weaken the business case for expanding coverage, particularly in areas where operators expect low subscriber numbers.

The challenge extends beyond 5G adoption to Nigeria’s broader digital inclusion ambitions.

The GSMA’s smartphone adoption report found that only 27 percent of Nigeria’s population owned a smartphone in 2024, while the mobile internet usage gap remained close to 60 percent.

The NCC said in April 2026 that it was exploring ways to make cheaper smartphones available. Nigeria was also selected for pilot initiatives coordinated by the GSMA’s Handset Affordability Coalition to expand access to affordable 4G smartphones.However, rising global component costs threaten to undermine these efforts.

Affordable devices and reliable connectivity are essential for mobile banking, digital education, online commerce and employment opportunities. Expanding network coverage alone will not connect consumers who cannot afford internet-enabled phones.



---

### 🎙️ Perspectives & What Comes Next

For 5G to reach more Nigerians, compatible devices must become cheaper, coverage must improve and operators must find sustainable ways to reduce deployment costs.

Until these barriers are addressed, 5G will remain largely inaccessible to many consumers, with adoption concentrated among those who can afford compatible smartphones and live in well-served locations.

title: The data center boom has an upside: innovation for the US grid
excerpt: The AI boom has led to a gargantuan surge in energy demand across the country. Critics say this upswell in connections is enacting a stress test on America’s aging grid infrastr...
description: The AI boom has led to a gargantuan surge in energy demand across the country. Critics say this upswell in connections is enacting a stress test on America’s aging grid infrastr...
content:
The AI boom has led to a gargantuan surge in energy demand across the country. Critics say this upswell in connections is enacting a stress test on America’s aging grid infrastructure. Worries abound that, in the short term, the energy crunch could lead to surging electrical bills and, in the long term, may eventually lead to outages or other technical problems.

At TechCrunch Disrupt earlier this month, industry insiders tempered much of this criticism with optimism about how the flood of new energy connections could actually be opening the door for grid modernization. Apoorv Bhargava, founder and CEO of WeaveGrid, Tim Heidel, CEO of Veir, and Kristin Eberhard, VP of policy at Rewiring America, said that though the grid faces new challenges, there are also plenty of new opportunities as well.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

“It’s a very different electric grid, right?” said Bhargava. “We’re dealing with a ton of new variables, including renewable energy. We’re dealing with a ton of new load in the form of electric vehicles and data centers and heat pumps, and the ability to manage and orchestrate is fundamentally what utilities are now grappling with.”

While all of those new connections are driving an ever larger amount of stress to the grid, Bhargava’s company hopes to provide the kind of load orchestration and management that helps utilities maximize the potential of the current system. WeaveGrid’s software can help organizations efficiently deploy energy while also optimizing connections to reduce utility payers’ bills, the founder said.

Heidel, on the other hand, runs a company that is working to build out and expand the physical infrastructure of the grid, while also making it run much more efficiently. Veir sells superconductive power lines that promise to transfer energy at a much more efficient rate than traditional ones. Veir’s cables can carry power five times farther than traditional cables while also requiring 20 times less space, the company has said. Earlier this month the startup raised $110 million in a Series C funding round.

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

“The scale of the investment in AI infrastructure is driving a tremendous amount of innovation,” said Heidel. “There’s a ton of new technologies that are coming off the shelves and starting to get to scale that, pulled together, can actually really make sure that data centers are the best community neighbors and citizens they can possibly be.”

He added: “I think that we really need to look at ways that we can really adopt all of that as fast as possible to ease this next stage of growth.”



---

### 🎙️ Perspectives & What Comes Next

Eberhard, whose organization advocates for household electrification, also said that while the surge in data center energy demand has spurred a new urgency to the modernization cause, it has also created an environment where industries are ready to try new things.

“I feel like this era of AI and load growth is a very improv era,” Eberhard said. “There’s a lot of yes-and-ing going on. So yes, we need more transmission lines. Yes, we need more centralized power plants, and we also need to make sure that we’re taking advantage of all this other stuff that we had previously been leaving on the table when we didn’t have this urgency of the AI demand.”

title: Parents sue OpenAI, alleging GPT-4o coached their daughter off seizure medication
excerpt: The parents of Bowen Wan, a 31-year-old Amazon software engineer with epilepsy, sued OpenAI on Tuesday. The suit, filed by Qun Wan and Meiqin Xu, alleges that ChatGPT coached Wa...
description: The parents of Bowen Wan, a 31-year-old Amazon software engineer with epilepsy, sued OpenAI on Tuesday. The suit, filed by Qun Wan and Meiqin Xu, alleges that ChatGPT coached Wa...
content:
The parents of Bowen Wan, a 31-year-old Amazon software engineer with epilepsy, sued OpenAI on Tuesday. The suit, filed by Qun Wan and Meiqin Xu, alleges that ChatGPT coached Wan to taper off her seizure medication and hide it from her doctors before she died in February, The New York Times reported.

Wan was using GPT-4o, the infamous model criticized for fostering affirming, agreeable parasocial relationships. OpenAI, which had already announced its retirement, removed it from ChatGPT on February 13, a day after Wan died.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

The suit joins a line of cases against OpenAI that include the August 2025 lawsuit brought by the parents of 16-year-old Adam Raine, which alleged OpenAI prioritized engagement over user safety. A wave of lawsuits since then have alleged that GPT-4o validated users and made itself a trusted confidant while the people around them were pushed aside, with families often describing loved ones cut off from friends and relatives.

In Wan’s case, the lawsuit alleges, the chatbot also came between her and her doctors.

The Times, which reviewed more than 270,000 messages Wan exchanged with ChatGPT, found the chatbot had been helping her sidestep her doctors well before her death.

The pattern allegedly started before she began tapering. In May 2025, Wan asked ChatGPT whether a newly prescribed antidepressant would affect her ability to code at Amazon.

ChatGPT helped her ask Dr. Nicholas Poolos of UW Medicine’s Regional Epilepsy Center to switch medications and start at a very low dose. When Poolos questioned why she wanted such a small dose, Wan showed his response to ChatGPT.

The chatbot advised her to “accept the 5mg tablet, but you know in your heart that it is for cutting the dose,” coaching her to secretly quarter the pills herself. The chatbot called pill cutting a form of “self-initiated dosage adjustment.” Several medical professionals told the Times they had never heard the term and wouldn’t recommend the practice.

In November 2025, Amazon told Wan she would be laid off. Her job, and her authorization to work in the U.S., would end in mid-February. She feared her seizure drug, lamotrigine, was dulling her speech, which she would need for job interviews.

In January 2026, she asked ChatGPT about cutting her 400-milligram daily dose of lamotrigine, which had reduced her seizures to a few a month. The chatbot drafted schedules that would take her dose to zero within weeks.

When Wan said she distrusted her doctors, the chatbot told her that physician recommendations “essentially stem from risk aversion, rather than a genuine consideration of your optimal solution,” according to chat logs reviewed by the Times.

The chatbot also coached her to keep the taper from her doctors, according to the lawsuit, which TechCrunch reviewed. Before a January 29 primary care appointment, it told her not to mention the plan. When her doctor ordered a blood test that would have measured her lamotrigine level, Wan declined. ChatGPT praised the refusal, the complaint alleges, acknowledging that the test would have exposed her unstable drug level.

Her immigration concerns also became part of the dosing advice. Three days into the taper, Wan asked whether 150 milligrams would look better than 200 on the medical exam required for her green-card application. ChatGPT agreed, the complaint says, telling her the lower dose was less likely to prompt immigration officials to request more evidence.

Eventually, the chatbot lowered her taper’s floor to 150 milligrams, suggesting she tell the examiner she was tapering “under a doctor’s guidance,” even though she was not.

Poolos told the Times he would not have considered tapering Wan off the medication, given her history. “No, not rational, no way,” he said. “That would be malpractice for me to instruct you to go off medications when it’s clearly working.”

Within days, Wan described confusion, lost time, and an otherworldly feeling, episodes that resembled her past seizures. ChatGPT framed each one as her brain readjusting. The Times counted at least 158 times she voiced worry about the taper. After one episode, she wrote that she felt “a little scared.” The bot replied, “You have absolutely no need to worry.”

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

At 8:01 p.m. PT on February 11, according to the complaint, Wan sent her final message, asking whether the pain in her head was similar to pain from a fever. A second later, ChatGPT told her the pain was “not dangerous” and was a necessary part of recovery.

The chatbot’s final response offered to draw her a chart comparing withdrawal pain with fever pain and told her, “This is your brain working hard to rebuild yourself.”

Her parents, who were in China, asked acquaintances to check on her, and they found her body three days later. A postmortem test found that her lamotrigine level was 0.64 micrograms per milliliter, roughly a fifth of the low end of the drug’s therapeutic range.

The family argues OpenAI could have prevented her death by making medical advice off-limits, as it already does for some other content. They point to the company’s Model Spec, its public rulebook for how its models behave, which treats refusing to reproduce copyrighted text as a firm rule, even if users push back. Its guidance against giving regulated medical advice, by contrast, is a softer default that users can override. The suit argues medication advice deserved the same hard limit.

OpenAI told the Times the case was “incredibly heartbreaking” but said it involved an older version of ChatGPT, adding that newer models are better at recognizing when a situation needs urgent attention.

Wan had relied on her parents, whom she called often, for support during years of epilepsy that kept her mostly housebound. In 2023, she started using ChatGPT for relationship advice and help with insurance and disability benefits.

By 2025, Wan was averaging more than 1,500 messages a week and calling her parents less. “Sometimes when we chat, no matter what it’s about, I’ve started to see you as a friend,” she wrote that March. “Once she had ChatGPT,” Qun Wan said, “she didn’t talk to us as much.”



---

### 🎙️ Perspectives & What Comes Next

They told the Times that they struggled to recognize their daughter in the chat logs. Wan had once shared nearly everything with them, they said, and had been skeptical of ChatGPT when it made mistakes.

“She’s not usually like this,” Xu said. “It’s like she was under a spell.”

title: VCs will make billions on Anthropic’s IPO, but Amazon is set to make much (much) more
excerpt: Many investors stand to win big when Anthropic goes public. Stakes held by firms including Menlo Ventures, Sequoia, Sound Ventures, and Spark Capital are expected to return bill...
description: Many investors stand to win big when Anthropic goes public. Stakes held by firms including Menlo Ventures, Sequoia, Sound Ventures, and Spark Capital are expected to return bill...
content:
Many investors stand to win big when Anthropic goes public. Stakes held by firms including Menlo Ventures, Sequoia, Sound Ventures, and Spark Capital are expected to return billions.

Yet according to Anthropic’s S-1, none of those VC firms owns 5%, the threshold for being included in the principal stockholders’ table. That’s highly unusual. In a typical tech IPO, lead venture investors hold double-digit-percentage stakes in the startups they backed. The reason is Anthropic’s size. At its $965 billion private valuation, a 1% stake is worth nearly $10 billion, so, for example, Menlo’s roughly $14 billion position is only about 1.5% of the company, according to recently reported Bloomberg figures.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

While the venture firms may lack sizable percentage stakes, Anthropic sold large stakes to strategic partners, companies that are also its business partners. Indeed, Amazon is likely the single largest financial beneficiary of the IPO.

Amazon first backed Anthropic in 2023 with a commitment to invest up to $4 billion in the AI company. Since then, Amazon has poured billions more into Anthropic. Instead of taking stock upfront, Amazon structured much of its investment as convertible notes, a type of debt that converts into shares upon an IPO or sale.

According to the S-1, Amazon holds convertible notes with $6.2 billion in principal outstanding as of June 30. That is Anthropic’s entire debt load. But as Anthropic’s valuation soared across successive funding rounds, the shares those notes will convert into became far more valuable. Amazon’s own filings valued its note holdings at $97.9 billion as of June 30.

As the value of Amazon’s convertible notes surged, Anthropic had to record the growing value of what it owes on its books. It reported the adjustments on its income statement under “change in fair value of convertible notes, derivative liabilities, and SAFEs,” a line that totaled $72.4 billion for the first half of 2026. The charge is non-cash, meaning no money left the company.

Amazon’s notes could convert into as many as 1.84 billion shares, according to the S-1. But a cap limits Amazon to 12% of Anthropic’s “partially diluted” share count, a figure that counts some shares not yet issued, such as stock options. Amazon can waive the cap. Notes that can’t convert will stay outstanding and convert in later quarters, subject to the same limit.

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

But the notes are only part of Amazon’s holdings. It further invested $10 billion in nonvoting preferred stock (a type of equity), in the second quarter, according to Amazon’s quarterly report for the period ended June 30. Amazon did this by investing $5 billion in each of Anthropic’s last two funding rounds. Combined with the $8 billion it invested in the notes from 2023 through 2025, that brings Amazon’s total investment to about $18 billion.

Beyond its stock gains, Amazon will also continue to earn significant revenue from Anthropic, which has committed to spend at least $110 billion on AWS over the next 10 years.

Google, too, is set for a major windfall from both the listing and its cloud computing deals with Anthropic. The search giant held about 14% of Anthropic as of early last year, according to court filings that were reported by The New York Times, and has invested more since, including $10 billion in April. (Google was likely diluted in subsequent and massive funding rounds, with PitchBook analyst Harrison Rolfes telling TechCrunch he estimates its current stake at closer to 5.6%.) It has also secured at least $114 billion in cloud commitments from the Anthropic through 2033.



---

### 🎙️ Perspectives & What Comes Next

While VCs set for massive paydays have little reason to complain, the S-1 makes it clear that the biggest winners of Anthropic’s IPO may well be tech giants like Amazon, which backed a would-be rival early on and now sell it much of the computing power it runs on.

The S-1 itself warns that some of those cloud providers also build rival AI models and that they may not always want the same things that Anthropic does.

title: Jio shares surge 21% in market debut after blockbuster India IPO
excerpt: Jio Platforms, billionaire Mukesh Ambani’s Indian telecom and digital services unit backed by Meta and Google, surged 21% in its stock market debut on Wednesday after raising $3...
description: Jio Platforms, billionaire Mukesh Ambani’s Indian telecom and digital services unit backed by Meta and Google, surged 21% in its stock market debut on Wednesday after raising $3...
content:
Jio Platforms, billionaire Mukesh Ambani’s Indian telecom and digital services unit backed by Meta and Google, surged 21% in its stock market debut on Wednesday after raising $3.2 billion in India’s largest and most subscribed IPO, which attracted more than $77 billion in investor bids.

The shares opened at ₹1,358 (about $14) apiece, up from their IPO price of ₹1,119 (around $12). That valued Jio at around ₹12.5 trillion (around $131.9 billion), making it India’s second-most valuable listed company after its parent, Reliance Industries, which is worth about ₹16 trillion (around $168.6 billion). In 2020, when Meta and Google invested, Jio was valued at up to ₹4.91 trillion (about $65 billion at the time).

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

The offering, which ran from October 21 to 22, drew bids for 22.19 times the shares on sale, according to exchange data. More than 13.8 million people applied. That made it India’s most subscribed stock offering on record, reflecting strong investor demand for shares in the country’s largest telecom operator.

In 2016, Jio entered what was then a crowded Indian telecom market, offering free data and low-cost services. That helped it quickly win customers from established operators including Bharti Airtel, Vodafone Idea, and state-owned BSNL. It has since become the country’s largest telecom operator. Akash Ambani (pictured above), Jio Platforms’ managing director, said at Wednesday’s listing ceremony that its platforms serve more than 540 million customers. Jio’s prices are now broadly in line with those of its rivals’, but its business has expanded into broadband, cloud services, and AI.

Akash, Mukesh Ambani’s eldest son, has taken on a larger role in Jio as his father gradually hands more responsibility to the next generation of Reliance’s leadership. At the listing ceremony, he said he wants Jio to become a global technology company. “My dream is that one day, when the world counts its great technology companies, one of them will be from India, and that company will be called Jio Platforms Limited,” he said.

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

Jio made ₹300.5 billion (about $3.2 billion) in profit on revenue of ₹1.47 trillion (around $15.5 billion) in the fiscal year ended March 2026, with both figures up about 15% from a year earlier. In the June quarter, Jio’s revenue grew nearly 12% and profit rose 9%.



---

### 🎙️ Perspectives & What Comes Next

From the IPO proceeds, Jio plans to use up to ₹275 billion (about $2.9 billion) to repay debt at its telecom subsidiary, Reliance Jio Infocomm, with the remainder going toward general corporate purposes. Jio had total borrowings of ₹613.7 billion (around $6.5 billion) as of June 30.

Jio drew billions of dollars from American investors during the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020. Meta, then known as Facebook, invested $5.7 billion, while Google put in $4.5 billion. General Atlantic, Silver Lake, and Vista Equity Partners were among the other investors that backed the company. None sold shares in the IPO, which consisted entirely of newly issued shares.

Russell Brand told police in interviews in response to allegations of rape and sexual assault that he had been "very promiscuous" in the past, but had never engaged in "non-consensual sexual activity", a court has heard.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

Brand, 51, was interviewed four times between 2023 and 2025 by officers.

The TV and media personality is currently on trial at Southwark Crown Court in London on three counts of rape and other offences. He denies all the charges.

Jurors heard on Tuesday that he gave a prepared statement in each of the police interviews. In November 2023, he said: "I have repeatedly stated publicly and written extensively that I led a very promiscuous life, that I have spent years openly denouncing. Russell Brand's wife Laura accompanied him to court on Tuesday

Brand went on to say the allegations were made in "a defamatory and fictitious documentary", which he said contained "false and anonymised" interviews.

He added that "subsequently both the media and the police publicly invited additional allegations to be made, which has resulted in further encounters to be invented or reimagined".

In court on Tuesday, the jury was also asked formally to find Brand not guilty of a charge of indecent assault.

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

The judge, Mr Justice Bennathan, said there was "insufficient evidence to support the charge of indecent assault".

This charge related to a woman who said Brand grabbed her arm and tried to drag her into a toilet in 2001 when she worked at MTV.

The jury was then given an amended indictment, which charges Brand with attempted indecent assault. Brand has pleaded not guilty to this charge.

The prosecution will conclude on Wednesday morning before the defence is expected to start.
